newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: DBS to increase shareholder value.
newsitem.headline: DBS to increase shareholder value.

text.p: DBS Bank Ltd will try to increase shareholder value with a steady increase in its dividend payout, president Ng Kee Choe said on Wednesday.
Ng told reporters after the release of the group's interim results that the bank has raised its interim dividend to nine Singapore cents in 1997 from eight cents in 1996.
It was the bank's first dividend increase in more than a decade. The last time the bank raised its dividend rate was in 1981, when it was increased to 16 percent from 15 percent.
"It is one way to reward shareholders and we hope to increase it steadily," he said.
Asked if the bank was concerned about the sharp premium its foreign shares have over the local shares, Ng said there had been discussions about the issue within the bank.
"We are obviously concern for all our shareholders and stakeholders...We have noticed the sharp premium of the foreign tranche."
However he said it was not an issue that could be decided by the bank alone. "Whether there is a need to maintain a foreign tranche is a policy question under the (Banking) Act."
Ng declined to say whether the bank had discussed the issue of maintaining foreign shares with policy makers.
Under Singapore banking laws, foreigners can only hold up to 40 percent stake in a local bank.
The existence of a smaller foreign tranche has resulted in hefty premiums for the shares. DBS foreign stood S$18.80 at the close of trading on Wednesday. The local shares were at S$8.80.
Foreigners also "know the value of DBS shares better", Ng said in explaining the huge discrepancy between the share prices.
DBS officials said the bank was conservative in its accounting policies and investments stated in its books were substantially below market value.

The net book value of its investment properties in 1996 was stated at S$925.74 million against a market value of S$2.13 billion while quoted investments were at S$5.02 billion against a market value of S$6.93 billion, said one official.
